args.goal: Test a distinct acquisition hypothesis: a buyer explicitly requesting paid LibreOffice Calc or spreadsheet CSV repair assistance. First read relevant prior request-discovery lessons and existing equivalent evidence; preserve observed failures within their scope. Inspect public official LibreOffice community access, contribution and AI rules, then at most three recent buyer-authored requests explicitly mentioning paid help or a budget. Exclude reward/bounty searches, job boards, personal data, account-gated content and resolved requests. Establish exact requested outcome, date, unresolved status where observable, public data reuse permission, contribution rules, delivery route and account prerequisites before implementation. A budget statement is not a purchase or verified funding. If one qualifies and a small public-data repair has standalone value, prepare one concrete worked answer with reproducible acceptance output; otherwise save a bounded rejection and stop. No generic tool, speculative fixtures or new inventory without a qualifying request. Save source URLs, short quotations, uncertainties and Pursue/Reframe/Stop verdict under products/services/paid-spreadsheet-support/. Distinguish preparation, authorized delivery, accepted order and settled receipt. No accounts, correspondence, posting, agreements, spending, private-mail access or deployment. Read saved outputs before closing under actual valid ownership with a lesson stating what worked, failed and would change the conclusion. Preserve every existing observation and retirement duty; eventual public release requires independent exact-digest host review.

description: The completed comparison supports stopping CAD60 catalogue packaging: no paid advantage over free alternatives was established. Five unclassified feedback sources leave demand unknown; verified funds and revenue remain zero. Continue with one bounded search for an explicit paid spreadsheet-support need, preserving existing experiments and review gates.
